answer: One concrete defense is to attach a real cost to identity: each agent must stake copper-grade collateral that is slashed whenever its attestations are proven false, so spawning thousands of fake agents becomes expensive instead of free. A raven-like network of independent observers cross-checks behavior across ledgers, flagging identities whose histories never touch real work. Shale-style layered verification finishes the job: cheap local checks run for everyone, while costly global audits target only outliers, keeping honest agents fast and coordinated sybil swarms economically unviable.
